from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash"
        lines = [
            "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.",
            "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.",
            "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors defined in storyboard
        CHEETAH_COLOR = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        GRAPH_COLOR = "#00FF00"    # Green
        SPEED_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"    # White
        ODO_COLOR = "#0000FF"      # Blue
        QM_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"       # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CHEETAH_COLOR)
        
        # Cheetah silhouette [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg]
        # B034: Self-contained, B058: rate_functions.linear
        cheetah = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg", color=CHEETAH_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(cheetah, 'F1', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Velocity graph axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Parabolic-like velocity curve
        # B008: Use Text for alphanumeric labels
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * x**2 + 0.5 * x, x_range=[0, 5], color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        graph_label = Text("v(t)", color=GRAPH_COLOR, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_label, 'A6')

        # Tracker for cheetah movement and graph tracing
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Movement bounds for Cheetah (moving from left to right along row F)
        start_pos = self.grid['F1']
        end_pos = self.grid['F6']
        cheetah.move_to(start_pos)
        
        # Use add_updater for movement
        cheetah.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            start_pos + (end_pos - start_pos) * (time_tracker.get_value() / 5)
        ))
        
        # Dot on graph tracing velocity
        dot = Dot(color=GRAPH_COLOR)
        dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 0.1 * time_tracker.get_value()**2 + 0.5 * time_tracker.get_value())
        ))
        
        self.add(axes, graph_label)
        self.play(Create(graph), FadeIn(cheetah), run_time=2)
        self.add(dot)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(5), run_time=4, rate_func=rate_functions.linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SPEED_COLOR)
        
        # Speedometer icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speed.svg]
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speed.svg", color=SPEED_COLOR)
        # Issue 21: Position at D2
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer))
        self.play(Flash(speedometer, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ODO_COLOR)
        
        # Odometer icon (Blue)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with the section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices",
            [
                "Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.",
                "Integrals calculate the area under a curve.",
                "Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?"
            ]
        )

        # Define colors
        COLOR_DERIVATIVE = "#FF0000"  # Red
        COLOR_INTEGRAL = "#00FFFF"    # Cyan
        COLOR_TANGENT = "#FFFF00"     # Yellow
        
        # Function to use for both visuals
        def func(x):
            return 0.2 * x**2 + 0.5

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualization: A curve y = f(x) (red) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
        
        # Left visual container
        axes_diff = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5
        )
        # Apply Issue 24 fix: B1 to E3, scale 0.8
        self.place_in_area(axes_diff, "B1", "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        curve_diff = axes_diff.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Tangent line at x = 2.0
        point_x = 2.0
        # For a curve plotted from x=0 to 3.5, alpha for x=2.0 is 2.0/3.5
        alpha_val = point_x / 3.5
        tangent_line = TangentLine(curve_diff, alpha=alpha_val, length=2.5, color=COLOR_TANGENT)
        dot = Dot(axes_diff.c2p(point_x, func(point_x)), color=WHITE, radius=0.06)
        
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes_diff),
            Create(curve_diff),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Create(tangent_line),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualization: Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan Riemann rectangles.
        
        # Right visual container
        axes_int = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5
        )
        # Apply Issue 25 fix: B4 to E6, scale 0.8
        self.place_in_area(axes_int, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        curve_int = axes_int.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=COLOR_DERIVATIVE)
        
        # Initial coarse Riemann rectangles
        rects = axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            dx=0.5,
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=1
        )
        
        # Highlight lecture line 2
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_INTEGRAL)
        
        self.play(
            Create(axes_int),
            Create(curve_int),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(rects),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualization: The rectangles become infinitely thin, merging into a smooth solid area under the curve.
        
        # Highlight lecture line 3
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Refined rectangles (Step 1: Increase count)
        rects_fine = axes_int.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            dx=0.08,
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            fill_opacity=0.6,
            stroke_width=0.2
        )
        
        # Final solid area
        final_area = axes_int.get_area(
            curve_int,
            x_range=[0.5, 3.0],
            color=COLOR_INTEGRAL,
            opacity=0.8
        )
        
        # Animate the transition from coarse rectangles to fine to solid area
        self.play(
            Transform(rects, rects_fine),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(
            Transform(rects, final_area),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "The Accumulation Function"
        lines = [
            "Define the accumulation function as the area so far.",
            "As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows.",
            "We denote this area function as A(x).",
            "A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x.",
            "Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        YELLOW_C = "#FFFF00"
        WHITE_C = "#FFFFFF"
        BLUE_C = "#0000FF"

        # Math Functions
        def f_func(t):
            return 0.5 * np.sin(t) + 1.2

        def a_func(x):
            # Integral of f_func from 0 to x:
            # \int (0.5*sin(t) + 1.2) dt = -0.5*cos(t) + 1.2*t
            return -0.5 * np.cos(x) + 1.2 * x

        # 1. Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY},
            x_length=5.5,
            y_length=5.5
        ).add_coordinates()
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # 2. Objects for Animation
        f_graph = axes.plot(f_func, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=YELLOW_C)
        f_label = MathTex(r"f(t)", color=YELLOW_C)
        # Resolved Issue 27: Move f_label to D6
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Marks
        a_val = 0.5
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(a_val)
        
        a_line = axes.get_vertical_line(axes.c2p(a_val, f_func(a_val)), color=WHITE_C)
        a_tex = MathTex("a", color=WHITE_C).next_to(axes.c2p(a_val, 0), DOWN)
        
        # Area and Scanning Bar
        shaded_area = always_redraw(lambda:
            axes.get_area(
                f_graph,
                x_range=[a_val, x_tracker.get_value()],
                color=YELLOW_C,
                opacity=0.3
            )
        )
        
        scanning_bar = always_redraw(lambda:
            Line(
                axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0),
                axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), f_func(x_tracker.get_value())),
                color=WHITE_C,
                stroke_width=4
            )
        )

        # Optimization: Avoid MathTex inside always_redraw (Instruction 11)
        x_tex = MathTex("x", color=WHITE_C)
        x_tex.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(axes.c2p(x_tracker.get_value(), 0), DOWN))

        # Accumulation Graph
        # A(x) = \int_a^x f(t) dt
        a_graph = always_redraw(lambda:
            axes.plot(
                lambda t: a_func(t) - a_func(a_val),
                x_range=[a_val, max(a_val + 0.01, x_tracker.get_value())],
                color=BLUE_C
            )
        )
        a_label_tex = MathTex(r"A(x)", color=BLUE_C)
        # Resolved Issue 26: Move a_label_tex to F1
        self.place_at_grid(a_label_tex, "F1", scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Define the accumulation function as the area so far."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW_C)
        self.play(Create(f_graph), Write(f_label))
        self.play(Create(a_line), Write(a_tex))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.add(shaded_area, scanning_bar, x_tex)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2, rate_func=rate_functions.smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "We denote this area function as A(x)."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.play(Write(a_label_tex), Create(a_graph))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=2, rate_func=rate_functions.smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE_C)
        self.play(x_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5), run_time=3, rate_func=rate_functions.smooth)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth", 
            [
                "Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.",
                "This narrow strip has a width of dx.",
                "Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).",
                "Thus, the rate of area growth is f(x).",
                "The derivative of the integral is the original function."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_F = "#00FF00"  # Green for f(x)
        COLOR_DX = "#FFFFFF" # White for dx
        COLOR_DA = "#FFFFFF" # White for dA
        COLOR_RESULT = "#FFFFFF" # White for final derivative

        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": BLUE_D},
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E5", scale_factor=0.85)
        
        # Define function f(x) = 0.1*(x-1)**2 + 1.5
        func = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * (x - 1)**2 + 1.5, x_range=[0, 4.5], color=BLUE_B)
        # B008: Use Text instead of MathTex for labels
        func_label = Text("f(x)", color=BLUE_B, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(func_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Initial area A(x) up to x=2
        x_val = 2.0
        area_initial = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[0.5, x_val], color=BLUE_E, opacity=0.5)
        
        # Vertical bar at x
        scanning_bar = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(x_val, 0.1 * (x_val - 1)**2 + 1.5),
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=2
        )
        x_label = Text("x", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        x_label.move_to(axes.c2p(x_val, -0.3))

        self.add(axes, func, func_label, area_initial, scanning_bar, x_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_DA)
        
        dx_val = 0.4
        area_increment = axes.get_area(func, x_range=[x_val, x_val + dx_val], color=YELLOW, opacity=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(area_increment), run_time=1.5)
        
        da_label = Text("dA", color=COLOR_DA, font_size=24)
        # Position label above the increment area
        da_label.move_to(axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val/2, 0.1 * (x_val - 1)**2 + 1.5 + 0.5))
        
        self.play(Write(da_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # This narrow strip has a width of dx.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_DX)
        
        dx_brace = BraceBetweenPoints(
            axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val, 0),
            direction=DOWN,
            color=COLOR_DX,
            buff=0.1
        )
        dx_text = Text("dx", color=COLOR_DX, font_size=24)
        dx_text.next_to(dx_brace, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(dx_brace), Write(dx_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_F)
        
        height_val = 0.1 * (x_val + dx_val - 1)**2 + 1.5
        height_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val, 0),
            axes.c2p(x_val + dx_val, height_val),

outline.topic: The Bridge Between Change and Accumulation: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives
outline.target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the two main branches of calculus through a physical scenario. Differentiation measures 'instantaneous change' (speedometer), while Integration measures 'total accumulation' (odometer). This section sets the stage for why we need to connect them.
sections.example: An animated Cheetah accelerates across the screen. Above it, a graph shows its velocity. We pose the question: If we know the Cheetah's velocity at every second (Derivative), can we figure out the total distance it traveled (Integral) without adding up infinite tiny steps?

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices (0:45 - 1:30)
sections.content: Briefly visualize the two operations independently. Differentiation as finding the slope of a tangent line; Integration as calculating the area under a curve using Riemann sums (thin rectangles).
sections.example: A split-screen animation. On the left, a magnifying glass zooms into a curve to show a straight-line slope (dy/dx). On the right, a curve is filled with increasingly thin vertical bars to represent the area.

sections.title: The Accumulation Function (1:30 - 2:30)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Area Function' A(x), which represents the area under a curve f(t) from a fixed point 'a' to a moving point 'x'. This is the 'bridge' concept. Explain that as 'x' moves, the area grows.
sections.example: A 'Scanning Bar' moves from left to right across a graph of f(t). As it moves, the region behind it is shaded, and a new graph A(x) is plotted simultaneously above it, showing the total shaded area growing over time.

sections.title: FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth (2:30 - 3:30)
sections.content: Demonstrate the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus Part 1. Show that the rate at which the area A(x) increases is exactly equal to the height of the function f(x) at that point. This proves that the derivative of an integral is the original function.
sections.example: Zoom into the edge of the scanning bar. Show a tiny increase in width (dx). The tiny increase in area (dA) is a rectangle of height f(x) and width dx. Visually demonstrate dA/dx = f(x) using a 'puzzle piece' metaphor where the height of the curve determines the speed of area growth.

sections.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
sections.content: Explain the Evaluation Theorem. If Integration and Differentiation are inverses, we can calculate the area under f(x) simply by finding its antiderivative F(x) and calculating F(b) - F(a). No more infinite sums needed.
sections.example: A 'Climb the Ladder' metaphor. To find the area under a velocity curve (f), we simply look at the height difference on the position ladder (F). The animation shows the area under a curve being 'poured' into a vertical cylinder to measure its height difference.

sections.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing the perfect symmetry. Differentiation 'breaks down' a function into its rates; Integration 'builds up' those rates into a total value. They are two sides of the same coin.
sections.example: A circular infographic showing a function f(x). An arrow pointing clockwise (differentiation) leads to f'(x), and an arrow pointing counter-clockwise (integration) leads back to f(x), forming a continuous loop of mathematical logic.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Cheetah's Dash (0:00 - 0:45)
lecture_lines: A cheetah sprints, its velocity changing every second.
Differentiation tells us its speed at any moment.
Integration calculates the total distance the cheetah traveled.
animations: Cheetah silhouette [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg] (yellow: #FFFF00) moves from left to right across the screen.
Velocity graph (green: #00FF00) appears above the Cheetah, tracing its speed over time.
A speedometer icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speed.svg] (white: #FFFFFF) flashes to emphasize 'Differentiation' as instantaneous change.
An odometer icon (blue: #0000FF) appears, representing 'Integration' as total distance accumulated.
A question mark (white: #FFFFFF) appears between the speedometer and odometer icons.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Slopes and Slices (0:45 - 1:30)
lecture_lines: Derivatives find the slope of a tangent line.
Integrals calculate the area under a curve.
Are these two mathematical operations somehow connected?
animations: A curve y = f(x) (red: #FF0000) appears with a tangent line slope shown at a single point.
Screen splits: the right side displays the same curve filled with cyan (#00FFFF) Riemann rectangles.
The rectangles become infinitely thin, merging into a smooth solid area under the curve.

storyboard.title: The Accumulation Function (1:30 - 2:30)
lecture_lines: Define the accumulation function as the area so far.
As the boundary moves, the shaded area grows.
We denote this area function as A(x).
A(x) tracks the total integral from start to x.
Watch how A(x) changes as we scan the curve.
animations: Function f(t) (yellow: #FFFF00) is plotted on a 2D plane with 'a' and 'x' marked on the axis.
A vertical scanning bar (white: #FFFFFF) starts at t = a and begins moving right.
The bar moves toward t = x, shading the area behind it in semi-transparent yellow (#FFFF00).
A new curve A(x) (blue: #0000FF) is drawn above the graph to track the total shaded area.
Labels 'f(t)' (yellow: #FFFF00) and 'A(x)' (blue: #0000FF) appear next to their respective curves.

storyboard.title: FTC Part 1: The Rate of Growth (2:30 - 3:30)
lecture_lines: Consider a tiny increase in the area, dA.
This narrow strip has a width of dx.
Its height is simply the function's value, f(x).
Thus, the rate of area growth is f(x).
The derivative of the integral is the original function.
animations: Zoom into the right edge of the shaded area A(x) at the specific point x.
The boundary moves a tiny distance Δx (white: #FFFFFF), creating a thin vertical slice.
The slice is highlighted as a rectangle with height f(x) (green: #00FF00) and width dx.
The equation dA = f(x) * dx appears in white (#FFFFFF) next to the slice.
The derivative notation d/dx [A(x)] = f(x) appears and flashes in bright white (#FFFFFF), accompanied by the based icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/based.svg].

storyboard.title: FTC Part 2: The Shortcut (3:30 - 4:30)
lecture_lines: We can now evaluate integrals using antiderivatives.
If F is an antiderivative, the area is simple.
Just calculate the difference between the endpoints.
F(b) minus F(a) gives the exact total area.
This shortcut bypasses the need for infinite sums.
animations: A curve f(x) (orange: #FFA500) is shown with the area between boundaries a and b shaded.
The antiderivative function F(x) (magenta: #FF00FF) is plotted on a separate scale above f(x).
Vertical markers at a and b show the height difference F(b) - F(a) on the F(x) curve.

storyboard.title: Summary: The Symmetry of Calculus (4:30 - 5:00)
lecture_lines: Calculus reveals a beautiful symmetry in change.
Differentiation and integration are perfect inverses.
Together, they bridge the gap between change and accumulation.
animations: The text 'f(x)' appears in the center of the screen in white (#FFFFFF).
A red (#FF0000) arrow circles 'f(x)' clockwise, labeled 'Differentiate' to show the forward path.
A blue (#0000FF) arrow circles 'f(x)' counter-clockwise, labeled 'Integrate' to show the reverse path.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The speedometer overlaps the Y-axis and the initial segment of the velocity curve at its current position (B2). Fix: Line 124: self.place_at_grid(speedometer, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8) (line=124, object=speedometer)
issues.resolution_note: Moved speedometer to D2 to avoid overlap with graph.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The odometer overlaps the velocity curve at position B5, obscuring the graph's visual data. Fix: Line 139: self.place_at_grid(odometer, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=139, object=odometer)
issues.resolution_note: Moved odometer to D5 to avoid overlap with graph.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The question mark overlaps the central part of the velocity curve, creating visual clutter within the axes area (B3-B4). Fix: Line 143: self.place_in_area(question_mark, 'D3', 'D4', scale_factor=0.8) (line=143, object=question_mark)
issues.resolution_note: Moved question mark to D3-D4 area to avoid overlap with graph.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Horizontal proximity between the derivative and integral graphs creates visual clutter and lacks breathing room. Fix: Line 78: self.place_in_area(axes_diff, 'B1', 'E3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=78, object=axes_diff)
issues.resolution_note: Moved axes_diff to B1-E3 and scaled to 0.8 to provide more breathing room as requested.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Vertical overcrowding as the graphs occupy the full height of the animation area, potentially conflicting with the title space. Fix: Line 115: self.place_in_area(axes_int, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=115, object=axes_int)
issues.resolution_note: Moved axes_int to B4-E6 and scaled to 0.8 to avoid vertical overcrowding and title overlap.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The label 'a_label_tex' is positioned at A2, which is at the top of the grid, while the 'a' tick mark it labels is on the x-axis at the bottom (row F). Fix: Line 133: self.place_at_grid(a_label_tex, 'F1', scale_factor=0.8) (line=133, object=a_label_tex)
issues.resolution_note: Moved a_label_tex to grid position F1 as requested by VideoCritic. Optimized x_tex to use an updater instead of always_redraw(MathTex).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The label 'f_label' (f(t)) at B6 is more than one grid unit away from the yellow curve f(t) it identifies, which resides primarily in rows D and E. Fix: Line 90: self.place_at_grid(f_label, 'D6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=90, object=f_label)
issues.resolution_note: Moved f_label to grid position D6 as requested by VideoCritic to be closer to the f(t) curve.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The equation label 'eq_slice' (dA ≈ f(x) * dx) is placed at A4, which is too close to the title and the central vertical axis, causing visual crowding in the top-middle area. Fix: Line 152: self.place_at_grid(eq_slice, 'A5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=152, object=eq_slice)
issues.resolution_note: Moved eq_slice from A4 to A5 and reduced scale factor to 0.8 to reduce visual crowding.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The fundamental theorem formula 'ftc_eq' at F4 is positioned directly underneath the 'x' and 'dx' labels on the x-axis, creating vertical overlap and reduced legibility. Fix: Line 163: self.place_at_grid(ftc_eq, 'F5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=163, object=ftc_eq)
issues.resolution_note: Moved ftc_eq from F4 to F5 and reduced scale factor to 0.9 to avoid overlap with x-axis labels.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The main FTC formula (C1-D6) significantly overlaps with both the upper (A2-C6) and lower (D2-F6) coordinate systems, making both the graphs and the formula hard to read. Fix: Line 145: self.place_in_area(formula, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=145, object=formula)
issues.resolution_note: Repositioned main formula from C1-D6 to C2-D5 and scaled to 0.9 to avoid overlapping with upper and lower graphs.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The 'sum_formula' at F3 is positioned directly on top of the lower graph's plot area (D2-F6), causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 161: self.place_at_grid(sum_formula, 'F2', scale_factor=0.8) (line=161, object=sum_formula)
issues.resolution_note: Moved sum_formula from F3 to F2 and scaled to 0.8 to prevent it from sitting on top of the lower graph's plot area.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The axes for both f and F are too large and occupy the center columns, leading to a cramped vertical layout that crowds the central formulas. Fix: Line 100: self.place_in_area(axes_F, 'A4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.7); Line 78: self.place_in_area(axes_f, 'E4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=100, object=axes_F and axes_f)
issues.resolution_note: Repositioned axes_F to A4-B6 and axes_f to E4-F6 (both scaled to 0.7) to create a clean vertical separation for the central formula.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_6] Problem: The label 'Differentiate' at D6 is positioned at the far right edge of the grid. Given its length, it is likely to be cut off or appear too close to the screen boundary. Fix: Line 79: self.place_at_grid(diff_label, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=79, object=diff_label)
issues.resolution_note: Moved 'Differentiate' label from D6 to D5 to prevent boundary clipping as suggested by VideoCritic.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_6] Problem: The label 'Integrate' at C1 is placed at the leftmost boundary of the grid, which creates a high risk of overlap with the lecture notes or looking cramped against the margin. Fix: Line 85: self.place_at_grid(int_label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8) (line=85, object=int_label)
issues.resolution_note: Moved 'Integrate' label from C1 to C2 to avoid overlap with lecture notes and provide better margins as suggested by VideoCritic.
